title: Fish Florentine
description: Fish Florentine is a classic Continental dish featuring pan-seared white fish fillets served over a creamy Florentine spinach base, topped with rich Mornay sauce and baked until golden for an elegant restaurant-style presentation.

ingredients.title: For the Fish
items: White fish fillets (halibut, cod, sole, or sea bass) – 4 pieces (180–200 g each, skinless & boneless)

ingredients.title: For the Mornay Sauce (Cheesy White Sauce)
items: Gruyère or Parmesan cheese – 50 g, grated
Dijon mustard – ½ tsp (optional, for depth)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Fish
steps: Pat the fish fillets dry.
Drizzle with lemon juice, season with salt and white pepper.
Heat olive oil and butter in a pan over medium-high heat.
Sear the fillets for 2–3 minutes per side until golden but just undercooked in the center (they will finish in the oven). Set aside.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Make the Florentine Spinach
steps: In a sauté pan, melt butter. Add shallots and garlic, cook until fragrant.
Add spinach, sauté until wilted.
Stir in cream, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Cook until creamy but not watery. Keep warm.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Prepare the Mornay Sauce
steps: In a saucepan, melt butter, stir in flour to make a roux.
Gradually whisk in warm milk until smooth.
Add cheese, whisk until melted and velvety.
Season with salt, pepper, and mustard if using.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Assemble & Bake
steps: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
In individual gratin dishes or a large baking dish, spread a layer of spinach Florentine.
Place seared fish fillets on top.
Spoon Mornay sauce generously over fish.
Sprinkle extra cheese.
Bake for 8–10 minutes until bubbling and golden on top.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Plating (Restaurant Style)
steps: Place each fillet with its spinach base at the center of a warm plate.
Drizzle lightly with olive oil.
Garnish with microgreens, a lemon wedge, and a delicate Parmesan crisp if available.
Serve with a side of duchess potatoes or buttered asparagus for a complete fine dining plate.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve with a side of duchess potatoes or buttered asparagus for a complete fine dining plate.

chefTips: For Michelin-level refinement, you can pipe the spinach base neatly into a ring mold before topping with fish and sauce, ensuring precision and elegance on the plate.
